implemented_capabilities.capability: Interval (valid_from/valid_to) temporal graph planner from snapshot series
implemented_capabilities.notes: Pure, DB-free function that diffs consecutive snapshots into node_open/node_close/edge_open/edge_close ops. Append-only history: closing a window stamps valid_to, never deletes; content changes (body_hash) close and reopen a new version and re-point incident edges to the new version; renames are detected by qualname equality plus Jaccard feature similarity >= 0.8 with plausibility guards and emit RENAMED_TO edges.

implemented_capabilities.capability: As-of (time-travel) queries with window predicate on every node and edge
implemented_capabilities.notes: Every MATCH adds n.valid_from <= $t AND (n.valid_to IS NULL OR n.valid_to > $t) for each node and relationship on the walk. Reverse CALLS is hard-capped at two explicit hops plus IMPORTS; all reads go through ro_query.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Deterministic temporal verdict with provenance-citing proof chain
implemented_capabilities.notes: No LLM. risk = 2*live dependents + 3*importing modules + changes in 30d + 2*authors; thresholds <=6 safe, <=15 care, else risky (explicitly a demo-tuned heuristic). Each proof-chain step cites the commit (sha, date, author) or the edge-walk at time t that produced it. Returns NEED MORE INFO instead of guessing when target or repo is ambiguous.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Honest-failure data-access discipline (read-only handle, 503 when DB down)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Agent code can only run GRAPH.RO_QUERY, so it cannot mutate the graph; unreachable DB raises a 503-mapped error rather than answering from files. Password redacted from repr/errors.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Python source parsing into modules, classes, functions, calls and imports
implemented_capabilities.notes: ast-based extraction with best-effort call-target resolution (unresolved callees are skipped); sampler walks git log/ls-tree/show read-only to build weekly-sampled snapshots.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Graph writer with UNWIND batches and chunked remote ingest API
implemented_capabilities.notes: Node writes are MERGE on (id, valid_from) and idempotent; edge opens are plain CREATE, so re-ingesting duplicates edges (documented by the author). Remote ingest endpoints accept raw ops from the client.

graph_models_and_cypher: Labels: Repository, Module, Class, Function, Person, Commit. Edges: DEFINES, CALLS, IMPORTS, MODIFIED{change,timestamp,commit}, AUTHORED, IN_REPO, RENAMED_TO{similarity}. Every node and edge carries valid_from/valid_to (epoch seconds, NULL = open) plus uid on edges. External imports are stub Module nodes with id prefix module:<repo>:$ext:. Cypher patterns: UNWIND batch MERGE (n:L {id, valid_from}) SET n += props; MATCH ()-[e]->() WHERE e.uid = row.uid SET e.valid_to; UNION-based label branches because FalkorDB lacks label disjunction; STARTS WITH/ENDS WITH/CONTAINS since there is no regex. Indexes on (Function|Module|Class).{id,valid_from}, Person.email, Repository.name, Commit.id. No APOC/GDS.
algorithms: Snapshot-diff to interval-operations planner with append-only version windows (timetrace/ingest/ingest.py:plan_ingest)
Content hash (sha256 over canonicalised signature) to decide node version rollover (ingest.py:body_hash)
Edge re-pointing after node version rollover so edges never outlive the version they were pinned to (plan_ingest, 're-point edges' section)
Rename detection by same qualname + Jaccard feature similarity >= 0.8 + same-dir/same-basename plausibility + file-appeared/vanished corroboration (ingest.py:similarity, _plausible_move)
As-of 2-hop reverse-CALLS blast radius with per-hop validity windows (graph/queries.py:_callers)
Open-window counting across commit timestamps in Python instead of N queries (graph/queries.py:timeline)
frontend_interfaces: Static UI ui/index.html + ui/app.js + ui/styles.css: repo timeline scrubber, module list at time T, ask box, verdict card, proof chain (served by FastAPI StaticFiles)
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: No LLM and no conversational memory. The 'agent' is a fixed pipeline: parse question -> resolve target -> presence at t -> blast radius -> churn -> owners -> verdict + proof chain. The graph itself is the memory (versioned history of code, who modified what, when).
tests_present: 6 pytest files, ~65 test functions (test_agent 12, test_e2e_local 8, test_ingest 18, test_parser 9, test_queries 11, test_sampler 7). The planner and parser tests are DB-free; test_queries and e2e need a local FalkorDB.
security_findings: timetrace/ingest/ingest.py:539-563,630,640,652 + timetrace/api/main.py:288-312 - Cypher injection: write_ops interpolates op['label'] and op['kind'] into query text with % formatting, and POST /api/ingest-ops passes client-supplied ops straight through with no auth and no allowlist (arbitrary graph write/delete)

timetrace/api/main.py:197-250 - POST /api/ingest accepts an arbitrary server-side directory path (snapshots_dir) and reads manifest.json and <sha>.json from it (path-controlled file read), unauthenticated, and writes to the configured FalkorDB
timetrace/api/main.py:262-285 - /api/diag-net performs DNS lookup and a raw TCP connect to the configured DB host (config-driven, not user-controlled, but unauthenticated network probe)
timetrace/ingest/ingest.py:597-598 - CREATE INDEX statement built with f-string from module-constant labels/properties (constants only)

timetrace/graph/queries.py:94-127,306-323 - labels interpolated into Cypher via f-strings but taken from a fixed tuple or from _label_for() which only returns Module/Function/Class; ids and times are parameters (safe)
timetrace/sampler/sampler.py:26-30 - subprocess.run(['git','-C',repo_path,*args]) list form, no shell; repo_path is caller-supplied (CLI/path), args are fixed git subcommands
No authentication or CORS config at all on the API; edge inserts are non-idempotent so repeated POSTs duplicate edges (data-integrity risk)
No hard-coded secrets: credentials come from .env/OS env and CI secrets; no eval/exec/pickle (parser uses ast.parse only).
duplicates_or_overlaps: Overlaps blast-radius traversal (code call graph), software dependency intelligence, and lineage/temporal-validity modelling (version windows, RENAMED_TO lineage). Complements kanchan0505/GraphHacks (freshness policy) with a real interval-validity data model.
evidence_drift_relevance: HIGH - the only repo in this batch with a true append-only valid_from/valid_to interval model, as-of queries that apply the window to every node and edge, version rollover with edge re-pointing, rename lineage edges and commit-cited proof chains; directly strengthens temporal validity, supersession (version close/reopen) and provenance in an Evidence Drift Cascade.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: Domain-agnostic in structure: it turns any ordered series of {nodes, edges} snapshots into idempotent-for-nodes open/close operations with content-hash change detection, closing windows instead of deleting, and edge re-pointing. Pair it with queries.py:_win for the as-of predicate. Only the node/edge schema (module/class/function) is code-specific.
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: none for the planner (stdlib only); FalkorDB only for FalkorWriter and queries

strategy_rationale: The interval planner and window-predicate query builder are a reusable temporal-validity layer for Kairos evidence, and are MIT-licensed. Generalise the node/edge schema, fix op-label allowlisting and make edge opens idempotent (MERGE on uid) before reuse.
